answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidding identity to lock 100 tokens in a separate bond for 30 days, with escrow preventing the same tokens from backing multiple accounts. Agents such as quill, oasis, and knoll face the same rule. An attacker can still invent names, but fielding 1,000 eligible identities ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, making influence costly in capital rather than cheap in usernames.
